solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Backed pound like this economist

indicators.note: something backed is put in reverse, so the word for pound is read from its end

parts.note: to lam is to beat or pound

explanation.surface: An economist whose ideas were driven back by a pounding currency.
explanation.walkthrough: MAL (LAM backed) + THUS gives Thomas Malthus, the English population theorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Malthus was the English scholar famous for his theory of population growth outrunning food supply.

clue.text: Mark a short distance in front of a large animal

indicators.note: placed ahead of, so the earlier pieces come first in the down answer

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, an old German currency
L for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone marking out a small gap ahead of a big beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A large animal' reads as one phrase, but 'a large' is wordplay and 'animal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mammal is a warm-blooded creature that suckles its young, one broad class of the animal kingdom.

clue.text: After lie, briefly show true colours

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is clipped and loses its final letter

parts.note: very in its old sense of real or true, as in 'the very man'

explanation.surface: After a fib, someone finally owns up and shows their real nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show true colours' is an idiom that tempts you to take the whole phrase as the definition; only 'colours' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform or colour scheme of a company, servant or vehicle fleet.

clue.text: Stew over answer to a contentious question

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so this word comes first

parts.note: a hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat under sliced potatoes
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone stewing over how to respond to a thorny question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like a verb meaning to fret, but it is the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an issue so controversial that nobody wants to handle it, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: Drawing with help from supporter, keeping client involved

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An artist sketching with the aid of a backer who keeps the customer engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stencilling is producing a design by painting through cut-out shapes, a kind of drawing or decoration.

clue.text: Group of Scouts put on uniform for assembly

indicators.note: one piece is put on, that is placed after, the other in the across entry

parts.note: flat as in even, constant, uniform
Cub Scouts are organised in packs

explanation.surface: A troop of Scouts dressing in uniform for a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' suggests a gathering of Scouts; here it is the putting together of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-pack furniture is sold in pieces in a flat box, ready to be put together at home.

clue.text: Regularly fall over some ice

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A warning that people often slip over on icy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating ice detached from the main pack.

clue.text: Feast loudly with salsa dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

explanation.surface: A noisy party celebrated with Latin dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' wants to be a homophone signal, but it is just letters to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls' Day, 2 November, is a Christian feast commemorating the faithful departed.

clue.text: In favour of miscellaneous couple going topless with me and others?

definitions.text: In favour of miscellaneous couple going topless with me and others?

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter, which in a down answer sits uppermost

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

explanation.surface: A semi-naked pairing with anyone and everyone, enthusiastically endorsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a topless couple pairing off with all comers paints the indiscriminate behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Promiscuous means having many casual sexual partners, indiscriminate in choosing them, as the scene describes.

clue.text: Arrive in the nick of time and make the grade all right!

definitions.text: Arrive in the nick of time

parts.note: to cut it is to succeed or measure up

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes in just in time and passes, to general relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it fine is to leave almost no margin of time, arriving just before it is too late.

clue.text: Stay in contention with endlessly enthusiastic whippersnapper

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky young person

explanation.surface: A veteran trying to stay competitive alongside an eager young upstart.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep up is to remain level with rivals rather than falling behind in a race or contest.

clue.text: Europeans holding positive vote retained something like CAP

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the others between them

explanation.surface: European voters backing a motion to keep the Common Agricultural Policy.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP in capitals poses as the EU's Common Agricultural Policy; it is just a peaked cap.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn to keep glare from the eyes, much like the peak of a cap.

clue.text: Children's game that may hint at golf?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playground ball game
second meaning, cryptic: a description of where the NATO alphabet's golf sits in the word piggy

explanation.walkthrough: Golf is G in the radio alphabet, and G is the middle letter of PIGGY, so the game's name literally describes that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Piggy in the middle is a playground game where one child tries to intercept a ball thrown over their head.

clue.text: Pave the way for power with revolutionary decree

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel government's edict prepares the ground for seizing control.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede something is to come before it, much as a forerunner clears a path for what follows.

clue.text: Unfairly achieve desired results on woodwork placement scheme?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: change the rules mid-contest to suit yourself
second meaning, literal: relocating the frame of a football goal

explanation.surface: A cheat gets their way through a scheme to relocate some carpentry.
explanation.walkthrough: In football slang the woodwork is the goalposts and crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes changing the conditions of a contest unfairly once it is under way, to secure a preferred outcome.

clue.text: Skimpy costume a greatcoat conceals

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A heavy overcoat hides a revealing outfit underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or insufficient in amount, the same sense as skimpy.

clue.text: Caught in fight after turning up for boozy event

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
in a down entry, turning up means the word runs upward, read backwards
one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight
C for caught, the cricket scorebook abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone arrested in a scuffle after showing up for a drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like an arrest; it is the cricket abbreviation, and 'turning up' is a real phrase hiding its own reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a tour of several bars in one evening, drinking at each, a decidedly boozy outing.

clue.text: Broadcast for church service

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like the religious one; it is a branch of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The air force is one of the armed services, alongside the army and navy.

clue.text: Points for attention if holding company changes direction

indicators.note: changing direction means the combined letters run the other way
the outer word holds the other inside it

explanation.surface: A firm that changes strategy has new things to concentrate on.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci, plural of focus, are central points on which interest or attention is concentrated.

clue.text: What's techy up to, struggling to input data quickly?

indicators.note: the letters are struggling, thrashing out of their order

explanation.surface: Asking what an irritable person is doing, fumbling at a keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Techy here is a variant of tetchy, irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch-type is to use a keyboard without looking at the keys, which is fast for entering text.

clue.text: Top year rearing horse, the largest animal of its kind

definitions.text: the largest animal of its kind

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: a rearing horse rises upward, and in a down entry that reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A champion year for a big horse rearing up.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara, a South American rodent, is the biggest rodent alive, which the definition hints at cagily.

clue.text: Capital street parking wholly in front of shopping centre

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed ahead of the last one

parts.note: P for parking, as on road signs
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Directions to a city road with parking right outside the retail complex.
explanation.walkthrough: Pall Mall is a London street known for its gentlemen's clubs; 'capital' means London.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall Mall runs through St James's in London, and capital is the setter's way of saying London.

clue.text: Chance event in which criminal traps one lot of detectives and headless coppers

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside
without a head, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes police

explanation.surface: A crime story where a crook catches police officers by happy accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police; here it is the small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A coincidence is a striking concurrence of events happening by chance without causal connection.

clue.text: Two different rings encircling first moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: the two words surround the other, one on each side

parts.note: a call is a ring on the phone, O is a ring shape
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Twin rings round the first of Jupiter's moons.
explanation.walkthrough: The rings are CALL (a phone ring) and O; 1ST becomes IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is the second-largest of Jupiter's satellites, discovered by Galileo in 1610.

clue.text: Red-light woman?

parts.note: surface: a woman working in a red-light district
setter's reading: a woman whose hair is a light shade of red

explanation.walkthrough: Red-light suggests a district of prostitution; read it as hair that is red and light in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberry blonde is a pale reddish-gold hair colour, and the phrase also names a woman with such hair.

clue.text: A universal god: that nameless thing with unknown power

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal viewing
it is the pronoun for an unnamed thing
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A cosmic deity, an unnamed something possessing mysterious power.
explanation.definitionFit: Authority is the right or capacity to command, which is a form of power.

clue.text: Deacon is excited to become a bishop

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A deacon thrilled at the prospect of promotion to the episcopate.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese, as opposed to an assistant or suffragan bishop.

clue.text: Urge that man to chase wife

indicators.note: to chase is to come after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: W for wife, as in genealogies
the pronoun for a male person

explanation.surface: Someone encouraging a man to pursue his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urge' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden impulse or fancy, a passing urge to do something.

clue.text: Artist to become held up by unexpected gift

indicators.note: held by means kept inside the other piece

parts.note: manna from heaven is an unexpected benefit

indicators.note: held up in a down entry means raised, reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to get, as in get angry, is to become

explanation.surface: A painter about to be delayed by a surprise present.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Mantegna was a fifteenth-century Italian Renaissance painter famous for foreshortened perspective.

clue.text: Powerful leader celebrity's half upset

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so read from bottom up
half means only one half of the word is affected, the first two letters

parts.note: a star is a celebrity; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A mighty boss whose famous friend is somewhat disgruntled.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of STAR is turned over; the rest stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the Russian emperor, and the word now names any person with great power over an area.

clue.text: Film Queen Elizabeth II?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a female star of the movies
second meaning, playful: the woman at the head of the nation

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the late Queen is described whimsically as the country's foremost woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading lady plays the principal female role in a film; the monarch was literally the lady who led.

clue.text: Forge bars or girders, primarily, yielding this metal in different form?

indicators.note: what is left is a symbol, which must be written in another form, its full name
to bar something is to exclude it, so letters are struck out of the word
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

explanation.surface: A smith working bars and girders into new shapes in a foundry.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip OR and G from FORGE and FE is left, the chemical symbol; written out in a different form that symbol is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fe is the chemical symbol for the element, from Latin ferrum, so the metal's full name is the answer.

clue.text: Pass round semi cooked goose

indicators.note: the outer word goes round the other

parts.note: the Simplon is an Alpine pass between Switzerland and Italy

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for handing round half-cooked poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose' is the fool sense, as in 'you silly goose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple Simon, the nursery-rhyme character, stands for a gullible fool, which a goose also means.

clue.text: Piece of rigging from sea holiday?

parts.note: the main is poetic for the open sea
a stay is a visit or short holiday

explanation.surface: A yachting holiday where something from the boat's gear goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainstay is the forestay running from the mainmast, a rope that braces part of a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Let out advance payment to shrink

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
to contract is to get smaller

explanation.surface: Someone paid in advance to take in a garment, though 'let out' suggests the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' and 'shrink' look like tailoring opposites; 'let out' means hand work to another firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To subcontract is to pass part of a job on to another party, to farm it out.

clue.text: Series of trees

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the England-Australia Test cricket series
second meaning: a group of a familiar hardwood species

explanation.walkthrough: A run of tree-related items is suggested; the cricket series is named after a mock obituary that burned the bails.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the trophy contest between England and Australia, and ash is a common deciduous woodland species.

clue.text: Great success due to Republican's New Model Army

indicators.note: a new model is a reworked version, so these letters are refashioned

parts.note: an army is a military force

explanation.surface: Victory attributed to Cromwell's New Model Army, the Parliamentarian force of the Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Model Army phrase is broken up: 'New Model' signals the jumble, 'Army' alone gives the force.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour de force is a feat of outstanding skill, an impressive achievement.

clue.text: Heard course of travel cut short, not having a spanner under one's car?

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, giving a different spelling
not having means a letter is left out

explanation.surface: A frustrated mechanic with no wrench to reach beneath the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' is not the tool but a thing that spans, a bridge, here a platform under a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighbridge is a platform scale set in the road, over which vehicles are driven to be weighed.

clue.text: Canteen dining attendant clearing out last of scampi with courage

indicators.note: clearing out means removing that letter from the word
last of means only the final letter is taken

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve

explanation.surface: A café waiter bravely clearing away the scampi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canteen' looks like a dining hall; here it is a flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a soldier's or hiker's flask for carrying drinking water.

clue.text: Presenter entertaining me with gag in the final stage

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a TV host presents a show

explanation.surface: A TV host tells the setter a joke at the end of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke; it is the retching sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The home stretch is the last part of a racecourse before the finish, hence the closing phase of anything.

clue.text: Monster? Er… Run in the opposite direction!

indicators.note: the letters run the opposite way, right to left

parts.note: to go is to run, as an engine does

explanation.surface: Someone stammering on spotting a beast and being told to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a classic fairy-tale beast.

clue.text: Audible row avoided: a source of visible upset

indicators.note: audible means as heard, so the words are spelt as other words that sound alike

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to duck something is to dodge it

explanation.surface: A noisy quarrel narrowly averted, though someone still looks distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow in the surface; it is a row of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: The tear duct produces the tears that show someone is upset, so it is where crying comes from.

clue.text: I don't like that second husband coming in back door in nonslip footwear

indicators.note: these pieces come into the other word
back means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Complaining about a second husband slipping in by the back door.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughshod horse has shoes with projecting nails to stop it slipping, hence the idiom ride roughshod.

clue.text: Joiner placing typical suburban house by cut-off settlement

indicators.note: cut off means its last letter is chopped away

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a staple of British suburbs
a colony is a settlement abroad

explanation.surface: A carpenter building a commuter house next to an isolated village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter; here it is a punctuation mark that links clauses.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses in a sentence.

clue.text: Kit's packaging lays prepared for future skipper, perhaps

indicators.note: packaging wraps around the contents

parts.note: Kit and Chris are both short for Christopher

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A sailor's gear is packed and ready for the next captain.
explanation.walkthrough: A skipper is a kind of butterfly, so 'future skipper' is one still in its pupa.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysalis is a pupa, the stage before an adult butterfly emerges, and skippers are small butterflies.

clue.text: Improved aim, seizing opportunity after dismissing opener

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold within

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, sent away

explanation.surface: A batsman's aim got better once the opening batsman was out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' and 'dismissing' suggest cricket; they only remove the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhanced means made better or greater in quality, value or extent.

clue.text: Police fine deceitful son brought to court

parts.note: F for fine, as on pencils
a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard

explanation.surface: Officers penalise a dishonest young man hauled before the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Squad is a London police unit dealing with armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flying Squad is a branch of London's Metropolitan force, the Sweeney in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Fancy a fruit Tango opened by servants

indicators.note: opened by means that piece comes first, at the front

parts.note: Tango is T in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: An invitation to try a fruit-flavoured Tango soft drink served by staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British fizzy drink, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something imagined, a product of fancy, as in a figment of the imagination.

clue.text: Encourage users with ear twists

indicators.note: twisting turns the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cheering up customers by tweaking their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure is to give confidence, to comfort and hearten, which is to encourage.

clue.text: Fellow accepting National Trust's role of responsibility

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A man taking on duties for the National Trust, the British heritage body.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on the mantle is to assume a role or responsibility, the cloak symbolising the office.

clue.text: Live current activated signal

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: An electrical warning that a live current has been switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a fire or light set up as a warning or guiding sign.

clue.text: Old king's private, large hotel for taking in Olympics?

indicators.note: the letters around take the other word inside

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
Hotel is H in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier staying at a big hotel during the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilgamesh was a legendary ruler of Uruk, hero of the ancient Mesopotamian epic.

clue.text: WC Fields's first turns as comedian

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter is kept
turns means the word runs the other way

explanation.surface: W.C. Fields, the American comic actor, has his first stage turns.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields was the comedian's name; split, WC is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a jester or clown, a professional comedian in old courts.

clue.text: Potentially dangerous competition that sounds like a charity fun run!

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as another phrase

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts, so a race for them is a charity run

explanation.surface: A race that sounds like harmless fundraising but is something risky.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech alms and arms sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An arms race is a contest between nations to build up weapons, which risks war.

clue.text: Hotels in opposite directions

parts.note: north and south are compass opposites

explanation.surface: Hotels located at opposite ends of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are small hotels or pubs offering lodging, so they are hotels by another name.

clue.text: Woman's pro-European statement?

parts.note: EU is the European Union, which the speaker backs
what such a supporter would say of it: that it is pleasant

explanation.surface: A woman declares her support for Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A pro-European might say 'EU nice', which spells the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a woman's given name, from Greek meaning good victory.

clue.text: Smash hit at concert hall to arrive at club

indicators.note: smashing breaks into pieces that are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smash-hit song at a concert hall gets the crowd to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash hit' reads as one phrase; 'Smash' alone signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlton Athletic is a professional football club from south-east London.

clue.text: Now end is in sight for inequality at last

indicators.note: is in means placed inside the other letters
at last means only the final letters of these words are kept

parts.note: the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: An optimistic claim that inequality may finally be over.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable and current, so 'now' as an adjective in modern slang for the latest thing.

clue.text: Inactivity that may follow love-in

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word that completes an old flower name beginning love-in

explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-idleness is an old name for the wild pansy, as in A Midsummer Night's Dream; a love-in is a hippy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness means doing nothing, being inactive or lazy.

clue.text: A little laughter observed about bishop in yesterday's news

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman chuckling at what he saw in old newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone whose fame is over, a person no longer relevant like old headlines.
